multiple chip model which qib has. Instead rely on the value which
exists already in the device data (dd).

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
u16 qpt_mask;
```
```c
if (qpt_mask && ((qpn & qpt_mask) >> 1) >= dd->n_krcv_queues)
```
```c
offset = find_next_offset(qpt, map, offset, dd->n_krcv_queues);
```
Reason:
The global variable `qpt_mask` was used to determine the behavior of the QPN allocation logic, which did not account for multiple devices. This could lead to incorrect QPN values being generated when multiple instances of the driver were in use, as the global state would not be unique to each device, causing conflicts and incorrect operations.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
u16 qpt_mask = dd->qpn_mask;
```
```c
offset = find_next_offset(qpt, map, offset, dd->n_krcv_queues, qpt_mask);
```
Reason:
The patch removes the global `qpt_mask` and instead retrieves the `qpn_mask` from the device-specific data structure (`dd`). This ensures that each device uses its own mask value, thus supporting the multiple chip model and preventing conflicts between different instances of the driver. The updated `find_next_offset` function now takes `qpt_mask` as a parameter, ensuring that the correct mask is used for each device.
